stories.headline: Drivers limited to 27-lap tyre stint as rule reintroduced for Qatar Grand Prix
stories.summary: Formula 1 drivers will be limited to a total of 27 laps on each set of tyres they use at next weekend's Qatar Grand Prix.
stories.body:
Formula 1 drivers will be limited to a total of 27 laps on each set of tyres they use at next weekend's Qatar Grand Prix.

Tyre manufacturer Pirelli said the restriction is necessary due to the high energy loads, thermal stress and tread wear experienced at the Lusail circuit, which is made up of a series of high-speed corners that have the potential to induce failures.

Assuming the race runs its full 57-lap distance, the restriction will ensure each driver makes at least two pit stops.

Under F1's normal tyre rules, only a single pit stop is necessary to comply with the regulations for a dry race.

It is the third time in four years that Pirelli has implemented a limit on the number of laps its tyres can complete at the Lusail circuit.

In 2023 the limit was 18 laps, in 2024 no limit was applied and last year the limit was 25 laps.

Pirelli said the slightly higher limit for 2026 was made possible "by the lower load levels recorded so far on the current generation of cars and by a further reinforcement of the tyre construction."

- Max Verstappen promoted to Las Vegas GP pole as Kimi Antonelli drops to sixth

- Hamilton and Leclerc suffer shock Ferrari double blow in Las Vegas qualifying

- Russell reignites Verstappen rivalry: 'Somebody has got to stand up to that guy'

The lap count on the tyres is cumulative over the weekend, meaning any laps completed in practice or qualifying are included in the limit of those tyres should they be reused in the race.

Reconnaissance laps, formation laps and any laps completed after the end of the race will not be included.

Last year's 25-lap restriction resulted in McLaren making a strategic error when its drivers Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri failed to take advantage of a Safety Car period to make their first pit stop, costing the team a likely victory and allowing Max Verstappen to take the three-way title battle down to the final round in Abu Dhabi.

stories.headline: Will Mauricio Pochettino start strongly at Man United? What his career stats say
stories.summary: Before Mauricio Pochettino leads Manchester United, how did his debuts at his previous teams go?
stories.body:
Mauricio Pochettino is here, and the new Manchester United boss has some match to introduce himself with a trip to face great rivals Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

Pochettino has taken over the sacked Michael Carrick but finds United in the relegation zone, one point behind newly-promoted Coventry City, after 10 games of the Premier League season.

Pochettino, though, is used to big bang starts to his club management tenures. Here, we take a look at how he fared on debut at each of his five previous clubs, and what the stats throw up for his first 10 games at each club.

Pochettino's start at Espanyol
Pochettino's debut as Espanyol boss, his first-ever match as head coach of any kind, was against crosstown rivals Barcelona, managed by Pep Guardiola, in Jan. 2009. Against all odds, Espanyol managed a 0-0 draw (they would then lose the away leg the following week 3-2).

In what probably serves as a heartening example for United fans, he had only been able to take two training sessions before that match (on the afternoon before the game and the morning of) where he instructed the players to press Barça high and leave them one-vs-one at the back.

He lined them up in what is now his trademark 4-2-3-1:

Carlos Kameni

Sergio Sanchez | Dani Jarque | Nicolas Pareja | Greg Beranger

Roman Martinez | Moises Hurtado

Nené | Valdo | Jose Callejon

Luis Garcia

It was a tough start to his managerial career, though. He was already Espanyol's third manager of the season, they were battling relegation when he joined and he managed to win only one of his first 10 matches (five draws, four losses) before stabilising over the remainder of the season to have a record of 53 wins, 38 draws and 70 defeats at a win rate of 33%.

The first win of his career, impressively, came vs. Guardiola's Barça in La Liga (in the 17 years since, Espanyol have beaten Barcelona just once more) and a run of eight wins in the last 10 league games saw Espanyol finish 10th that season.

From his first 10 games to his overall record at the club, he improved marginally on every parameter below.

Comparing Pochettino's first 10 games to his overall record at Espanyol:

Goals per game: 1 vs. 1.1

Goals against per game: 1.5 vs. 1.4

Possession: 48% vs. 52% (league only figures)

Clean sheet percentage: 10% to 29%

Pochettino's proving ground at Southampton
Pochettino's last few matches at Espanyol were poor and they separated by mutual consent with the Catalans bottom of LaLiga in late Nov. 2012. His stock as manager was high, though, and he was appointed as Southampton boss mid-Jan 2013, becoming just the second Argentine to manage in English football after cult hero Osvaldo Ardilles.

His Saints debut saw them draw 0-0 with David Moyes' Everton at St. Mary's, with Rickie Lambert at the end of the best chances created in the match (he hit the post, saw a header cleared off the line).

Southampton also lined up in a 4-2-3-1:

Artur Boruc

Nathaniel Clyne | Maya Yoshida | Jos Hooiveld | Luke Shaw

Morgan Schneiderlin | Jack Cork

Jason Puncheon | Guly de Prado | Gaston Ramirez

Rickie Lambert

His first win in England came vs. defending champions Manchester City, and in his first (and last) full season (2013-14) with Southampton, he led them to eighth, their highest league position in a decade.

He started well with the Saints with four wins in 10 (three draws, three defeats) and more or less maintained that progression in stats throughout his reign to finish with a win rate of 38% (23 wins, 18 draws, 19 defeats).

Comparing Pochettino's first 10 games to his overall record at Southampton:

Goals per game: 1.6 vs. 1.5

Goals against per game: 1.3 vs. 1.2

Possession: 54% vs. 57% (league only figures)

Clean sheet percentage: 30% to 35%

Pochettino became elite at Tottenham Hotspur
In May 2014, Pochettino joined the team for a stint that would mark him as one of the top managers in Europe across five-and-a half entertaining seasons. His first match was a Premier League clash with West Ham United, which he won 1-0 thanks to a 93rd-minute Eric Dier goal.

Spurs lined up in a 4-2-3-1:

Hugo Lloris

Kyle Naughton | Eric Dier | Younes Kaboul | Danny Rose

Etienne Capoue | Nabil Bentaleb

Erik Lamela | Christian Eriksen | Aaron Lennon

Emmanuel Adebayor

Spurs reached the final of the League Cup in his first season and finished fifth in the league. The season was marked by Pochettino making several academy graduates and young signings into regular first-teamers, including Harry Kane (who had been given his first Premier League start by Tim Sherwood).

Over his tenure, he'd lead Spurs to several record highs including the 2019 Champions League final and a second-placed finish in 2017-18 (highest since 1962-63).

In his first 10 games, Spurs won five (three draws, two defeats) and he maintained a solid record overall with 159 wins, 62 draws and 72 defeats at a 54% win rate as they improved as an attacking side.

Comparing Pochettino's first 10 games to his overall record at Tottenham:

Goals per game: 1.6 vs. 1.9

Goals against per game: 0.9 vs. 1.1

Possession: 54% vs. 59% (league only figures)

Clean sheet percentage: 40% to 34%

Pochettino managed superstars at PSG
Pochettino joined another former team in Paris Saint-Germain mid-way through the 2021-22 season as he replaced current England boss Thomas Tuchel and he started with a 1-1 draw vs. St. Etienne in Jan. 2021.

Instead of his usual 4-2-3-1, Pochettino lined his team up in a 4-3-3:

Keylor Navas

Colin Dagba | Thilo Kehrer | Marquinhos | Mitchel Bakker

Idrissa Gueye | Marco Verratti | Ander Herrera

Ángel Di María | Moise Kean | Kylian Mbappé

Within a fortnight of joining PSG, Pochettino won his first ever trophy as PSG beat great rivals Marseille to win the French Super Cup, but that adjustment in starting formation highlighted just how much Pochettino had to tweak his trademark high-pressing style to accommodate the big names in the squad -- which would also include Neymar and Lionel Messi during his reign.

Despite the draw on his debut, Pochettino had a flying start to life in Paris winning eight of the first 10 games (one draw, one defeat) before dipping to a (relatively) saner 66% win record with 55 wins, 15 draws and 14 defeats. He also won Ligue 1 and the Coupe de France.

Comparing Pochettino's first 10 games to his overall record at PSG:

Goals per game: 2.1 vs. 2.2

Goals against per game: 0.6 vs. 0.9

Possession: 63% vs. 63% (league only figures)

Clean sheet percentage: 60% to 39%

Pochettino's whirlwind return to England with Chelsea
Pochettino returned to England, and London, to take charge of Chelsea in May 2023. His first match saw yet another draw, a thrilling 1-1 vs Jürgen Klopp's Liverpool thanks to an Axel Disasi equaliser

With the tinkering of PSG still fresh in mind, Pochettino went with an unusual 3-4-2-1 on his Chelsea debut, with current Man United midfielder Andrey Santos an unused sub in the matchday squad.

Robert Sánchez

Axel Disasi | Thiago Silva | Levi Colwill

Reece James | Enzo Fernández | Connor Gallagher | Ben Chilwell

Raheem Sterling | Carney Chukwuemeka

Nicolas Jackson

It was a short-lived reign, though, and despite being on a five-game winning run at the end of the league season, Pochettino left Chelsea in May 2024 after clashing with management over strategy and recruitment. While he was there, Pochettino led Chelsea to the League Cup final and had Chelsea playing some end-to-end attacking football.

Pochettino won five games in his first 10 games there (two draws, three defeats) and ended with a very similar 51% win rate and a record of 26 wins, 11 draws and 14 defeats, with his side becoming less defensive and more goal hungry as the season wore on.

Comparing Pochettino's first 10 games to his overall record at Chelsea:

Goals per game: 1.4 vs. 2

Goals against per game: 0.8 vs. 1.5

Possession: 62% vs. 59% (league only figures)

Clean sheet percentage: 40% to 24%

Information from ESPN Global Research was used in this report.

stories.headline: 2026 NBA Cup: Schedule, format, groups, updates and more
stories.summary: Here's everything you need to know about the fourth annual in-season tournament, including the recent win by the Nuggets.
stories.body:
Which two teams will face off inside Hinkle Fieldhouse in Indianapolis for the 2026 Emirates NBA Cup?

This summer, the league unveiled the full group stage schedule for this year's in-season tournament, with action taking place every Friday from Oct. 30 to Nov. 27 and on special Cup nights during Thanksgiving week (Nov. 24-25).

After the New York Knicks became the first team to win the NBA Cup and Finals in the same season, can Jalen Brunson & Co. keep their championship run going? They'll have plenty of competition, specifically within the star-studded East Group B.

Here's what you need to know about the in-season tournament, now in its fourth year.

Jump to a section:

Schedule | Groups | FAQ

Denver Nuggets 133, Houston Rockets 124

The Nuggets haven't had the most consistent start to the season, but their clutch-time defense gives reason for hope. It was on full display as a shootout turned into a bit of a slog as the team outlasted the Rockets in Denver.

The Nuggets held the Rockets to just 21 points in the fourth quarter, continuing the trend of having the best defensive rating in clutch time this season. Usually that is combined with Jamal Murray, who is leading the NBA in fourth-quarter scoring at over nine points a game, but he had a more subdued offensive performance.

And with Murray scoring just 14, the Nuggets improved to 2-0 in the West Group A. They are in a neck and neck race with the Dallas Mavericks in terms of point differential.

Nikola Jokic scored 18 of his 26 in the third quarter (24 in the second half) and added 11 rebounds and seven assists. His matchup with Alperen Sengun went as advertised, as Sengun posted a triple-double (28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists) despite ending as a minus-13.

For the Rockets, it's an age-old issue, although Houston showed signs of being a more organized outfit with Fred VanVleet running the show in the fourth. But Kevin Durant attempted just nine shots in 35 minutes, continuing a seasonlong theme.

Part of that is Durant, who famously refuses to force his offensive game in the face of double-teams from 30 feet out. But for the Rockets to have such a potent weapon, it feels like they're allowing him to be taken out of games.

For a team to have 31 assists and two facilitators keeping everyone involved (Sengun and VanVleet, nine assists each), it's somewhat puzzling that Durant doesn't get the ball more late in games when the offense begins to stall.

On the positive side, one can see the strides being made by Amen Thompson and Jabari Smith Jr. Both were efficient and game-changing with their athleticism despite the final result. -- Vincent Goodwill

Toronto Raptors 105, Detroit Pistons 102

Scottie Barnes took the game in his hands all night for the Raptors, finishing with 29 points, five rebounds and five assists. His lefty layup was the go-ahead basket in the final minute as the Raptors snapped a six-game losing streak, beating the Pistons 105-102 in Detroit.

Toronto is now 2-1 in Group A in the NBA Cup while Detroit falls to 1-1.

Barnes looked mighty comfortable, making his first nine shots -- his first miss was a tip-in dunk from an offensive rebound that popped out. But the most surprising performance from the Raptors came from Allen Graves, who scored 20 points and had 10 rebounds. He repeatedly moved Pistons out the way for offensive rebounds and putbacks, making the most of his first start.

Detroit, playing without Jalen Duren, Duncan Robinson and Ron Holland, had done a decent job of masking its lack of shot creation but played from behind most of the night. The defense that was so stout all of last season, and in the past two games, was a step slow and it showed.

The Pistons didn't get their first lead until late in the fourth quarter off a Kevin Huerter 3. Cade Cunningham hit a step-back 3 over Barnes' outstretched arms with 20 seconds left to put the Pistons up one, before Barnes came back on the next possession. Cunningham had a crucial turnover on the Pistons' last offensive possession, then set up Huerter for what could have been an improbable trip to overtime with a hard carom free throw that bounced right back to him.

Several trends were on display as the short-handed Raptors had trouble finishing the game. It was similar to back-to-back home losses to the Knicks where they could have closed New York out with more poise.

Detroit struggled without Duren at the rim on both ends, allowing the Raptors to shoot 55% from the field. John Collins continues to struggle in his role at center and played only 19 minutes while finishing with three points in the loss. -- Goodwill

NBA Cup FAQ: Everything to know
What is the format?

NBA commissioner Adam Silver has had a longstanding fascination with European soccer. Establishing an in-season cup competition within the NBA schedule came from soccer leagues having both a regular-season title, won by the team with the most points over the full year, and a separate tournament (or, in some leagues, multiple tournaments) that runs concurrently with the league season.

In England, for example, there are the various divisions -- led by the Premier League -- and also the FA Cup competition. But unlike those European leagues, which play their cup competitions outside of their league schedules, the NBA Cup is built in to the regular-season slate.

The 30 NBA teams are split into six five-team groups -- three featuring Eastern Conference teams and three comprising Western Conference teams -- with each team then playing one game against the other four in its group. The winner of each group, plus the team with the best record among the non-group winners, advances to the knockout stage of the competition.

How will this impact the regular-season schedule and standings?

Typically, the NBA sends out a full 82-game schedule in mid-August. Now, the league sends out only 80 games and leaves a gap of roughly a week to fill in later, depending on how the group stage of the NBA Cup plays out.

The two teams from the East and West that lose in the quarterfinals will play their 82nd game against each other. Meanwhile, the 22 teams that fail to qualify for the knockout rounds will have their final two games scheduled -- one at home and one on the road against others eliminated in the group stage.

The teams that reach the NBA Cup final will actually play 83 games -- though the championship game won't count toward the standings or any statistical markers. The four teams that reach the semifinals will have completed their 82 games and won't need any other games added to their schedule.

Any team that makes it to the semifinals will have that game moved later in the schedule to avoid back-to-back games. The NBA made this change in an effort to avoid having empty days on the calendar while attempting to minimize back-to-backs for all teams as much as possible.

Where are the semifinals and final being played?

In a shift from previous tournaments, the quarterfinals and semifinals will be played at home sites. The Dec. 11 title game, meanwhile, will move from Las Vegas to the storied Hinkle Fieldhouse in Indianapolis. NBA commissioner Adam Silver previously said the league was searching for "storied college arenas" to play host to the Cup final. (No venue has been announced for 2027.)

Why does the NBA Cup include regular-season games?

Before its launch, one of the main questions surrounding the in-season tournament was why any team would be incentivized to compete in it. The NBA ensured teams will be motivated by making every game part of the season and, as in-conference matchups, potentially important to playoff tiebreakers. If this had been set up like the cup tournaments in European soccer, there would have been nothing stopping NBA teams from opting out by sitting their top players for extra rest.

Which teams make up the groups?

To create the groups, the NBA put the 15 teams in each conference into five pots, separated by their finish last season. Pot 1 included the teams that finished in the top three in the regular-season standings, Nos. 4-6 in the standings went into Pot 2, Nos. 7-9 into Pot 3, Nos. 10-12 into Pot 4 and Nos. 13-15 into Pot 5. Does one group stand out the most from the others?

East Group B is a monster.

All five teams -- defending NBA Cup and Finals champion New York, Philadelphia, Cleveland, Miami and Indiana -- are among the favorites to win the conference in 2026-27. The group stage will also feature reunion games for LeBron James, when the 76ers face the Cavs and Heat. And after guard Tyrese Haliburton missed the entire 2025-26 season while rehabbing a torn Achilles, the Pacers will be back among the East elite and hungry to reach the title game in Indianapolis.

What do players get for winning?

In 2023, the first year the tournament was held, the players on the winning team received $500,000 each and the runners-up got $200,000. The losing players of the semifinals each got $100,000, and those ousted in the quarterfinals got $50,000. Now, in each subsequent year, the prizes will be slightly higher, as a result of negotiated raises year over year to keep pace with increases in the salary cap and basketball-related income as part of the most recent collective bargaining agreement between the NBA and the National Basketball Players Association.

Will anyone earn individual honors for their play in NBA Cup games?

There will be an MVP award, as well as an all-tournament team.

Will this have any impact on the playoffs?

Not beyond the games counting in the regular-season standings (and toward tiebreakers). The only playoff impact comes from the wins and losses accrued throughout the tournament. Though there was debate among league insiders about guaranteeing a playoff berth for winning the tournament, ultimately that idea (or any other to further incentivize teams) was not enacted.

Why is it called the Emirates NBA Cup?

The league struck a sponsorship deal with Emirates, the Dubai-based airline, to sponsor the tournament after its initial run. The NBA said last year that it went with the most basic titles for both the tournament and its trophy -- the "in-season tournament" and "NBA Cup" -- as a way to introduce the concept to fans. However, using such nondescript names had another clear advantage: It gave the league a blank slate in case it sold the naming rights for the tournament and cup to a sponsor and avoided the complications that could arise by naming them after someone (for example, late NBA commissioner David Stern, one possibility that had been floated before the tournament was officially unveiled).

stories.headline: Luis Gil, former AL Rookie of Year, cut by New York Yankees at tender deadline
stories.summary: Veteran starting pitcher Luis Gil, 28, a former American League Rookie of the Year, was cut loose by the New York Yankees, among 44 players who became MLB free agents when their teams declined to offer 2027 contracts by Friday's tender deadline.
stories.body:
Former AL Rookie of the Year Luis Gil was cut loose by the New York Yankees, among 44 players who became free agents when their teams declined to offer 2027 contracts by Friday's tender deadline.

A 28-year-old right-hander, Gil was voted the American League's top rookie in 2024 after going 15-7 with a 3.50 ERA in 29 starts. With a four-seam fastball that averaged 96.6 mph, he struck out 171 in 151⅔ innings but walked a major league-high 77.

Sidelined by a lat strain for much of 2025, he went 4-1 with a 3.32 ERA in 11 starts. Gil spent much of 2026 in the minors and was sidelined by right shoulder inflammation, going 1-2 with a 4.61 ERA in four starts and five relief appearances for the Yankees.

He had a $2,162,500 salary this year and would have been eligible for arbitration.

New York also chose not to offer a contract to reliever Fernando Cruz. The 36-year-old right-hander didn't pitch after Aug. 25 because of a partially torn ulnar collateral ligament. He said he would try to return from the injury without surgery.

Cruz went 4-6 with a 3.13 ERA and two saves in 61 appearances last season. He struck out 67 batters and walked 32 in 54⅔ innings.

Washington right-hander Josiah Gray, a 2023 All-Star, also was cut loose. Gray, who turns 29 next month, was limited to two games in 2024 because of a torn ulnar collateral ligament, then was limited to three September appearances this year because of a right flexor strain. He had been designated for assignment Tuesday.

Others non-tendered included St. Louis infielder Nolan Gorman, Cleveland outfielder/infielder/catcher David Fry, Minnesota outfielder Trevor Larnach and right-hander Bailey Ober, Seattle outfielder Luke Raley, Toronto outfielder Davis Schneider, San Diego left-hander JP Sears, Los Angeles Dodgers right-hander Jake Cousins, Tampa Bay right-hander Cole Sulser and Philadelphia outfielder Bryan De La Cruz.

All those players would have been eligible for arbitration had they been offered contracts, but instead they joined a market that included 183 players who became free agents after the World Series.

Among players facing the tender deadline, first baseman/outfielder Gavin Sheets agreed to an $11 million, three-year contract with San Diego that allows him to earn $1.5 million annually in performance bonuses for plate appearances. The 2028 and 2029 seasons are $4 million player options that give him the right to terminate the deal and become a free agent.

Thirty-five players agreed to one-year contracts:

• Baltimore right-hander Felix Bautista ($2.3 million).

• Boston second baseman Romy Gonzalez ($1.65 million plus $25,000 performance bonuses each for 300 and 350 plate appearances), infielder Andruw Monasterio ($1.4 million), outfielder Eli White ($1,325,000 plus $25,000 performance bonuses each for 200, 250 and 300 plate appearances) and second baseman Jahmai Jones (the higher of $950,000 or the 2027 minimum plus $150,000).

• Chicago White Sox catcher Joey Bart ($2.53 million).

• Cleveland right-handers Colin Holderman ($2,175,000) and Matt Festa ($1.5 million) and outfielder Blake Perkins (non-guaranteed at the higher of $950,000 or the 2027 minimum plus $150,000, with a $500,000 salary while in the minor leagues).

• Houston shortstop Nick Allen ($1.95 million) and left-hander Bennett Sousa ($1.26 million plus $20,000 performance bonuses each for 30 and 40 innings).

• Kansas City right-hander Randy Dobnak ($1.35 million).

• Angels outfielders Jose Siri ($2.5 million) and Alex Call ($2,175,000), left-hander Tayler Saucedo ($1.3 million) and right-hander Sam Bachman (the higher of $1.05 million or the 2027 minimum plus $140,000).

• Miami left-hander Andrew Nardi (the higher of $900,000 or the 2027 minimum plus $100,000).

• Milwaukee infielder Joey Ortiz ($2,525,000), left-handers Angel Zerpa ($1,195,000) and DL Hall (the higher of $1,037,500 or the 2027 minimum plus $237,500) and right-handers Ryan Walker (the higher of $1.1 million or the 2027 minimum plus $330,000) and Grant Anderson (the higher of $925,000 or the 2027 minimum plus $125,000).

• Minnesota right-handers Cole Sands ($1.19 million) and Tommy Nance ($925,000).

• Mets left-hander Cionel Perez ($1.95 million) and right-hander Austin Warren ($900,000).

• Philadelphia outfielder Derek Hill ($1.4 million), left-hander Tanner Banks ($1.3 million), catcher Rafael Marchan ($900,000) and right-hander Jordan Leasure ($835,000).

• Pittsburgh outfielder Akil Baddoo ($1 million in major leagues, $488,557 in minors).

• San Diego right-handers Jhony Brito ($810,000 in major leagues, $300,000 in minors) and Bryan Hoeing ($807,000 in major leagues, $403,500 in minors).

• San Francisco right-hander Camilo Doval ($6.3 million).

stories.headline: AFL Draft 2026: Grading the draft hauls for every club
stories.summary: The 2026 AFL Draft has been run, but which team won? ESPN's draft expert Jasper Chellappah has handed down five As and two Ds after this year's two-night affair.
stories.body:
The 2026 AFL Draft has been run and done, so let's get into grading each team's haul. Night one was headlined by a Brisbane points matching debacle, with the Swans landing Caylen Murray.

It flipped the script for teams down the order with the Saints and Pies landing their preferred prospects thanks to Brisbane's three-point miss on Murray.

On night two there was a clear directive from clubs to draft based on list need. With the crop of talent 15 past 40 so even this year, clubs were focused on specific roles that suit the modern game and it resulted in bolting mature-agers earning main list opportunities.

These draft grades aren't just based on the calibre of talent brought into the club - it was a lot easier for Port Adelaide and Carlton to land star youngsters than North Melbourne and Geelong. It takes into account live trading, value on each pick and positional fits at the club.

These are ESPN's draft grades for every club after the 2026 AFL Draft.

READ: 'No one saw it coming' - Inside the Swans' draft heist that landed a Lions Academy star

Adelaide
Pre-draft hand: 15, 32, 35, 43, 54

Selections: Toby Krasna (14), Xavier Ladbrook (34), Sam Tassone (44)
There was a clear plan from the Crows to address their transition ball movement, and they've done so here. Krasna is an outside midfielder that really came on this year with his class in space. He runs hard both ways, plays with flair on the ball and is incisive with his foot skills in the forward half.

Xavier Ladbrook will take time to develop as a 202cm key defender that needs time in the gym, but his running base and length gives him an exciting platform. It was rounded out with local dasher Sam Tassone who has some raw, developable traits with speed out of defence.

The Crows passed up Anthony Long after Geelong's bid on the NGA forward.

Grade: B-

Brisbane
Pre-draft hand: 21, 27, 28, 45

Selections: Kodah Edwards (27), Archie Van Dyk (28), Jackson Phillips (29), Archie Spencer (36)

We haven't seen a bid matching debacle quite like Brisbane's on night one when they fell three points short of keeping Caylen Murray. The Lions cornered themselves and found no trade partner on the clock.

It meant they unexpectedly carried three selections back to back early on night two, opting for two South Adelaide products in Edwards and Van Dyke as they addressed their midfield mix.

Edwards captained SA and has versatility to play on-ball or through the forward 50, while Van Dyk has the size and skill to develop rapidly in a professional environment.

Phillips looks a natural wingman at the next level with good ball use off both feet and disciplined running patterns. He looks most likely to play senior football early next year, and they rounded out with dashing defender Archie Spencer.

Grade: D

Carlton
Pre-draft hand: 13, 18, 31, 50, 59, 67, 73

Selections: Cody Walker (3), Harvey Spawton-Guy (32), Jackson Watkins (37), Ethan Herbert (46)

A nice mix of prospects for the Blues began with the arrival of Cody Walker early on night one. The gifted midfielder has Brownlow upside in his prime as a natural ball-winner that puts speed on the game with aggressive movement.

WA's Harvey Spawton-Guy will be looked at as a tall to develop at both ends of the ground - he competes superbly in the air and that attack on the footy bodes well. Jackson Watkins plays with power in the forward half as a smaller type and Ethan Herbert's upside as a ruck of the future is enticing with his ball-winning and skill around the ground a point of difference.

Grade: A-

Collingwood
Pre-draft hand: 11, 30, 63, 64, 65

Selections: Sam Gayfer (12), Gus Kennedy (31), Jordan Knapp (41), Koby LeCras (62)

This is some sort of result for the Pies. They had Gayfer circled on their board from a long way out and were delighted to find him available. His courage and strength in the air at a combine-record vertical leap will be a nightmare to defend.

Kennedy is one of the great characters of the class and plays with a lot of energy off halfback, while Knapp is an exceptional ball magnet through the midfield but will need to build size at the next level.

Rounding out a significant haul was one of the big sliders Koby LeCras. The nephew of premiership Eagle Mark, the 192cm forward can roam up wings with a big engine and is a beautiful kick around goals off his preferred left.

Grade: A

Essendon
Pre-draft hand: 1, 17, 25, 69, 75, 78, 80 (plus second round compensation pick)

Selections: Ethan Drever (2), Archie Elliott (17), Harvie Cooke (21), Jack Pickett (26), Blake Justice (55)

The Bombers had a lot of work to do on each night and they will come away happy with the draft haul. Drever is the perfect complement to previous drafts through the midfield as the outside speed and damage, rating him as the No. 1 player in the open pool.

They paired him with best mate Archie Elliott which produced the best moment of night one as he was pulled out of the crowd at Marvel Stadium. The small forward is an excellent aerialist and has a defensive edge to his game that appeals.

Harvie Cooke was the Talent League's best and fairest and will suit a high half forward role at the next level, while the 194cm Jack Pickett is the big upside swing in the second round as the most accurate set shot to come through the pathways in some time. He will take time as he rehabs a torn ACL and MCL.

The Dons rounded it out with NGA Blake Justice who will be a slow starter to pre-season with a hamstring, but the 192cm midfielder has a unique blend of speed, agility and height that is exciting to develop.

Grade: B+

Fremantle
Pre-draft hand: 19, 40, 58, 61, 68

Selections: George Dimer (18), Kane Johnston (42), Jake Medved (57)

The Dockers have some ready-made options to add depth on a flag tilt. They were delighted that Dimer got through a host of suitors late on night one, and he looms as an immediate Switkowski replacement. Dimer is ultra-clean below his knees at 173cm and sets up teammates selflessly.

Kane Johnston is a 24-year-old tall out of the WAFL that's played his best footy in the forward 50 but could be utilised in defence. His body is ready to compete and the athleticism is AFL level.

Fremantle pinched Jake Medved out of the Swans Academy to round out their night. The utility has played in just about every position this season but could be best used as a wingman with his ranginess and endurance base.

Grade: C+

Geelong
Pre-draft hand: 36, 55, 60

Selections: Lachie Hicks (38), Anthony Long (56), Zach Stevens (60)

This was a quintessential Cats draft. They entered late on night two and immediately took a swing on one of the best athletes in the draft. Hicks has the speed-endurance blend Geelong covets, covering big distances and racking up the ball all season for the Western Jets.

Anthony Long was one of five(!) academy prospects they bid on late. The Crows NGA prospect is Izak Rankine's cousin and brings sharp agility and forward 50 creativity at 184cm.

Finally, Zach Stevens was the classic local product pick out of South Barwon. He's possibly the fastest product to be drafted and as a half forward showed flashes in the VFL and at Talent League levels.

Grade: B

Gold Coast
Pre-draft hand: 8, 70, 72, 77

Selections: Leo Steed (10), Elliott Himmelberg (63), Jamarra Ugle-Hagan (64)

The Suns took one live pick to the draft via Ben King's compensation. They opted for the midfield option in WA's Leo Steed, whose clean hands, strong transition running and fantastic work ethic rocketed his stocks this year. Steed has balance and selflessness to his game.

They rounded out the draft with two rookie elevations.

Grade: C

GWS
Pre-draft hand: 9, 20, 26, 57

Selections: Ethan Matthews (6), Jake Eime (13), Andrio Sousa (45)

Matthews is the best academy prospect GWS has had since Tom Green, and the earliest they've ever taken in a draft. The Giants moved up as far as they could so their residual draft pick would sit in the teens and with that pick they opted for Jake Eime.

A very Giants-esque selection, the SA product is an aggressive rebounder off halfback with the dare to tuck the ball and take on opponents. He can finish off transition in the forward half with good disposal and forms an exciting combination with Lachie Ash.

On night two Andrio Sousa presented as a fantastic athlete to develop on a wing or forward flank, though in isolation trading pick 20 to the Power for a future second-rounder was a poor return.

Grade: B-

Hawthorn
Pre-draft hand: 29, 37, 66, 74

Selections: Benji Van Rooyen (30), Cooper Hodge (58), Keenan Boi (59)

The Hawks targeted a real list need with Van Rooyen, the younger brother of Melbourne's Jacob. He's a legitimate ruck size and uses his physicality in the air well, enjoying the best championships of any ruck this year playing for WA.

The Cats made sneaky bids on Luke's son Cooper Hodge and Keenan Boi, with the latter sliding through to make for a comfortable bid match. Hodge's best traits come in the contest where he's tough and aggressive, while Boi has a lot of power in the forward half.

Grade: C+

Melbourne
Pre-draft hand: 4, 14, 48, 51, 79

Selections: Mitch Harris (7), Lochie Burrows (15), Ben Forster (49), Kaie Sullivan (52)

The Dees had another two first-rounders to play with and opted for the top key defender in Harris. His form a SANFL League level to finish the season cemented his top-10 status and Melbourne will look to him and Disco Turner as the future combination in defence.

Lochie Burrows is one of the best characters in the draft and gives the Dees huge flexibility as a halfback or hard-nosed on-baller. Ben Forster is a role player swing late in the draft with the wingman running hard both ways and offering neat skills in space. Kaie Sullivan was the late-season boater out of the Stingrays after a huge finals campaign elevated his stock off half forward.

Grade: B

North Melbourne
Pre-draft hand: 33, 49, 62

Selections: George Gale (23), Seb Marsic (35), Aidan McCartney (54)

The Roos traded their future first-rounder to get in for George Gale, such was their plaudits of the hardened youngster. He runs hard as an outside midfielder and has the size to eventually transition inside, but looks like a disciplined role player that will allow others to shine early in his career.

Seb Marsic was a bolter on night two as a big, physical key forward. He kicked seven goals in a game that North's Ollie Griffin kicked four at the other end.

The Aidan McCartney bid was matched late on night two with the 195cm son of Jason finding his way to Arden St.

Grade: B-

Port Adelaide
Pre-draft hand: 7, 12, 22, 24, 34, 46

Selections: Dougie Cochrane (1), Clancy Snell (19), Wil Malady (20), Wil Antrobus (25), Gabriel Patterson (39), Angus White (47)

The draft of the year goes to Port Adelaide. Dougie Cochrane was only the start for them, but it was a big one with the consensus best prospect in the pool becoming Port's first-ever No. 1 pick.

Shrewd live trading landed picks 19 and 20 and they grabbed sliders. Clancy Snell is one of the best interceptors in the crop and at 197cm will play on a range of forwards. Wil Malady is an upside swing on the clear talent. The 190cm forward is athletic and brilliant in the air.

Wil Antrobus was an early call at pick 25 but fits a clear need out of defence. His left leg is lethal in open play and he can be relied upon to kick in. They finished off with local products - Gabe Patterson plays with power in the forward half while Angus White has rehabbed an ACL this year but adds speed through the midfield.

Grade: A+

Richmond
Pre-draft hand: 2, 5, 44, 76 (plus second round compensation pick)

Selections: Arki Butler (4), Harry Van Hattum (8), Noah Williams (22), Harry Franz (51)

Richmond landed open prospects at 1 and 3 in ESPN's Power Rankings. Arki Butler, the match-winning medium forward, and Harry Van Hattum, the standout ruckman, are upside swings into the future. Neither can be expected to hit the ground running fully next year but could spearhead the Tigers into a new era.

Noah Williams was a smart choice at 22 with his competitiveness through the midfield and in defence giving him the versatility to play early. Richmond finished their draft with Harry Franz, a high-flying 194cm defender out of SA that plays with physicality.

Grade: A+

St Kilda
Pre-draft hand: 10, 16, 41

Selections: Gustavo Teixeira (11), Tyson Bradley (16), Lewis Houndsome (43)

The Saints could not believe their luck when Brisbane didn't match on Caylen Murray and Gus Teixeira slid all the way through to 11. A genuine first overall pick chance at stages this year, Teixeira has power, class and upside in the forward half.

They nabbed another bayside product at 16 in Vic Metro MVP Tyson Bradley. At 195cm he should grow into the physical key defender that takes on the big forwards at AFL level.

St Kilda finished off night two with Lewis Houndsome, a big key forward that's played well through the ruck but struggled with injuries after a promising bottom-age campaign.

Grade: A

Sydney
Pre-draft hand: 6, 38, 39, 47

Selections: Caylen Murray (9), Brady Wright (40), Mitch Knevitt (48), Mason McGroder (61)

It was a bold and brilliant coup to land Murray, but it remains to be seen if he was best available for the Swans at that point. It's a clear list need with the departure of Nick Blakey in the off-season; Murray offers dash and class off halfback, being one of the most reliable distributors in the crop and offering midfield upside.

Brady Wright was prolific for Werribee in the VFL, and the 194cm goalkicker is a best 23 candidate next year after winning the Fothergill-Round-Mitchell Medal. They added to their mature-age pickups with delisted Cat Mitch Knevitt, whose size around the ball could prove valuable.

Mason McGroder didn't attract a bid until pick 61 which made matching a formality. The long jumper won silver at the U20s World Games in Oregon this year and presents as one of the best athletes to ever come into the AFL system.

Grade: B+

West Coast
Pre-draft hand: 3, 23, 56 (plus second round compensation pick)

Selections: Heath Mellody (5), Jake Soutar (24), Harper Banfield (65)

The pickups are solid for the Eagles, but the way they approached this draft is up for debate for a second straight year. Despite being armed with more list spots than any team in the competition thanks to assistance packages, they were once again caught out this week, not turning over enough primary list spots.

West Coast traded a valuable second-rounder into next year, receiving North's future first in the heavily-compromised 2027 draft -- Tasmania's first. As a result they only took the three picks this time around -- a disappointment for a rebuilding side -- all from WA.

Heath Mellody is the best WA prospect since Luke Jackson, providing the outside run and carry that clubs covet. He's an elite kick and fits alongside Harley Reid and Willem Duursma superbly. Jake Soutar is the readymade option and they went early on the 20-year-old. He's a natural interceptor at 190cm and will likely play on third talls next year.

They rounded out the night by taking father-son Harper Banfield with their natural selection after a bid didn't materialise. He's a strong-bodied midfielder with an elite endurance base.

Grade: D+

Western Bulldogs
Pre-draft hand: 42, 52, 53, 71

Selections: Khaled El Souki (33), Jack Riding (50), Sam Devers (53)

It was an uncomfortable wait through night one and early parts of night two for a bid on El Souki to arrive. The small forward NGA landed in an ideal part of the draft for the Dogs to match and the eruption from El Souki's family and friends was worth the wait. His physicality, left foot and goal sense gives him an elite platform to blossom at the Dogs.

The 26-year-old Jack Riding has toiled away with Werribee to earn this opportunity, and is drafted with a role for him in the forward 50. He's a beautiful crumber of the ball and has mixed it in senior football already.

Sam Devers is an upside play as a 189cm defender that straight lines the ball and puts speed on the game. He took time returning this year after a shoulder reconstruction.

Grade: B

stories.headline: Fantasy football Week 11 inactives: Who's in and who's out?
stories.summary: Updated inactives and analysis based on the latest reports and official announcements leading up to kickoff.
stories.body:
Biggest injury concerns for Week 11
Players with early starts
Carson Beck, QB, Cardinals (back): Beck popped up on Thursday's injury report with a back injury. He has dealt with this issue throughout the season and currently appears to be unlikely to play in Week 11. Josh Johnson would be next man up and is purely a two-QB format option for those who are desperately in need of a bye week/injury replacement. In either event, Trey McBride is the only Cardinals player who should be started with any confidence -- and even his value is diminished in this new-look Cardinals offense.

Dalton Kincaid, TE, Bills (thumb/ankle): Kincaid has not yet practiced this week and is doubtful for Week 11. With the Bills playing the Chiefs on Thanksgiving -- just four days after this game -- expect Buffalo to use caution here. If he sits, Dawson Knox becomes a deeper streaming option against a Dolphins team that has allowed the fifth-most TE fantasy PPG.

Don't forget to check these out: Mike Clay's Playbook | Week 11 Buzz

Week 11 Rankings | Matchup rankings for Week 11

Official Sunday inactives should begin coming in approximately 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff times: around 11:30 a.m. ET for the early games and 2:30 p.m. ET for the late-afternoon games.

Refresh often for the latest information.

Jonathon Brooks, RB, Panthers (groin): Brooks is questionable for Week 11 but seems close to making his return after having practiced in full all week. He is worth adding if he is available on your league's waiver wire, but fantasy managers should take a wait-and-see approach. Chuba Hubbard remains an RB1 play.

Darren Waller, TE, Panthers (knee): Waller is questionable for Week 11 after limited practices Thursday and Friday. Waller is a TD-dependent streaming option. Some preferred TE plays are Mark Andrews and Chig Okonkwo. Waller should be used over Brenton Strange, Dallas Goedert and Mike Gesicki.

Kyle Monangai, RB, Bears (toe): Monangai is off the injury report, meaning he will play in week 11. He has not played since Week 4. Still, he is in the mix as a flex option due to a matchup against the Saints. New Orleans has allowed the fourth-most rushing yards to RBs, as well as the second-most RB fantasy points.

Caleb Douglas, WR, Dolphins (shoulder): Douglas had been limited at practice this week before elevating to full on Friday. He is off the injury report, meaning he will play in Week 11. He has seen eight targets in both of his last two games and has scored double-digit fantasy points in three of his four games since returning from injury. While he is more volatile with QB Kyle McCord, Douglas is in the flex conversation, especially given all the byes.

Jordyn Tyson, WR, Saints (chest): Tyson has been limited at practice this week and is questionable for Week 11. If he plays, he'd be a WR3 (with a lot more upside). Tyson saw a 38% target share and 50% air yard share last week in his first NFL game with no limitations. In a game in which the Saints will have to put up points, Tyson should be started.

DeVonta Smith, WR, Eagles (hamstring): Smith has practiced in full this week and is off the Eagles' practice report, meaning he is set to make his return in Week 11. He will be the top target for Joe Milton and the Eagles. While his production likely takes a hit without Jalen Hurts in the huddle, Milton does throw a good deep ball. That could lead to some big plays for Smith. He should be valued as a low-end WR2 in his first game back on the field. Dontayvion Wicks (ankle/foot) will not return this week for the Eagles.

Michael Pittman Jr., WR, Steelers (foot): Pittman has not played since Week 3 but is practicing in full this week. He seems on track to return this week. While that's a boost for those streaming Aaron Rodgers this week, I would take a wait-and-see approach with Pittman. Not only is it his first game back, but the Steelers have struggled to get consistent production from their receivers. This does make Germie Bernard, who has been unproductive as of late, a firm sit. The only Steelers receiver worth starting is DK Metcalf. Roman Wilson (hand) is also questionable for the Steelers.

Baker Mayfield, QB, Buccaneers (ankle): Mayfield returned to practice Thursday, which puts him on the right side of questionable. While Mayfield has not been a great fantasy option himself this season, his presence has elevated Tampa Bay's playmakers, especially Emeka Egbuka. Still, Mayfield is a streaming option this week against the Lions, who allow the second-most QB fantasy PPG.

Carnell Tate, WR, Titans (shoulder): Tate has been limited at practice this week, and while he is questionable, he is trending toward making a Week 11 return. From Weeks 3-7 (Tate's last five games), he had a 27% target share (11th highest) and a 45% air yard share (third highest). He was producing then and certainly could do so again in this new-look Titans offense that has averaged 39.5 passing attempts per game over the past two weeks. Tate is a WR3 with upside.

Players with late starts
Jaylen Waddle, WR, Broncos (concussion): Waddle has practiced in full coming out of the Broncos' bye week. He has been removed from the injury report and will play in Week 11. Waddle is a WR3 with upside in a favorable matchup against the Raiders. Las Vegas ranks in the top three in terms of the most yards and touchdowns allowed to wide receivers this season. With six teams on bye, it's worth taking a shot on Waddle this week.

Bhayshul Tuten, RB, Jaguars (ankle/foot): Tuten is off the injury report and will play in Week 11. He has been in and out of practice for the past couple of weeks but continues to play and be productive. Tuten has surpassed 20 fantasy points in three out of his last four games. If Tuten plays for the Jaguars, he should be started in fantasy football. It's worth noting that Chris Rodriguez Jr. (hand), who is the next man up, has also been limited at practice.

Brock Bowers, TE, Raiders (ankle): After exiting early in Week 10, Bowers returned to practice Thursday. He is questionable for Week 11. When asked if he will play this week, Bowers said, "We'll see," per ESPN reporter Ryan McFadden. If he suits up, he is an obvious must-start. If he sits, Michael Mayer is a TE1 worth starting in a favorable matchup. Denver has allowed the third-most TE fantasy PPG. Mayer is still a potential flex option this week if Bowers suits up.

Ladd McConkey, WR, Chargers (back): He has been limited at practice this week after missing the past two games because of a back injury. He is questionable, but even if he suits up, the risk of him leaving early is high. McConkey has played well when he has been able to stay on the field this season. The issue is that he has played just two full games. Because of that, fantasy managers should play it safe and look to get away from McConkey for the time being.

Isaiah Likely, TE, Giants (undisclosed): Likely wasn't seen at practice Friday with what John Harbaugh called a "minor injury." He was not on the injury report Friday and will be active Sunday. Likely has reached must-start status whenever he suits up.

Geno Smith, QB, Jets (ankle): Smith has been limited at practice before upgrading to full Friday. He is off the injury report, meaning he will play in Week 11. Smith is a QB2 against a Chargers defense that has been tough against QBs. Some streaming options I'd prefer over Smith are Bo Nix, Cam Ward, Mayfield and J.J. McCarthy.

Players on Sunday night
T.J. Hockenson, TE, Vikings (wrist): Hockenson was limited at practice this week before being upgraded to full participation on Friday. He is off the injury report and will play in Week 11. Consider him to be a low-end TE1, though I would rather play Mark Andrews or Chig Okonkwo. However, I would roll with Hockenson over Kincaid, Darren Waller or Brenton Strange.

Mike Evans, WR, 49ers (Achilles): Evans returned to practice in a limited fashion Thursday. That gives him a chance to suit up this week, even though he is questionable. If he plays, he would be a WR2 who carries both upside and risk. The upside has been clear. The risk is reinjury or struggling in a tough matchup against the Vikings, who have allowed the fifth-fewest WR fantasy PPG. If he sits, Deebo Samuel Sr. would be Brock Purdy's top wideout -- and a fantasy WR3.

Players on Monday night
Jacory Croskey-Merritt, RB, Commanders (groin): JCM appears likely to make his return from IR on Monday against the Bengals. Rachaad White has led this backfield in his absence, but I would anticipate Croskey-Merritt will handle the bulk of the ground work, with White as the passing-downs back -- a role that better suits him. Austin Ekeler is likely the odd man out.

Fantasy managers should ideally take a wait-and-see approach with Washington. However, with six teams on a bye, they may need to pivot to a Commanders RB. Either JCM or White would be deeper-league flex options. Croskey-Merritt brings a safer floor, but White has more upside since the Commanders could end up trailing and needing to throw a bunch in this one. However, it is worth noting that White was added to the injury report Friday (heel), which has his availability in question. If he were to sit, Croskey-Merritt would become a more appealing option, with Ekeler being an option in deep leagues.

Ruled out before Sunday

Kenneth Walker III, RB, Chiefs (groin): The Chiefs are big favorites this weekend against the Cardinals and will face the Bills on Thanksgiving, just four days later. They have a number of big games to come. Due to that, they are practicing caution and have ruled Walker out for Week 11. Emmett Johnson becomes a must-start RB1 with Walker out this week.

Omar Cooper Jr., WR, Jets (ankle/hip): Cooper has not yet practiced this week and has been ruled out for Week 11. Cooper has been banged up for a bit, so a week to recover will probably do him some good. He is worth stashing if you have the space on your bench. In his absence, expect Adonai Mitchell to see more targets. Mitchell should be considered a boom-or-bust flex option against the Chargers, who have allowed the sixth-most WR fantasy PPG.

Wan'Dale Robinson, WR, Titans (ankle): Robinson has been placed on IR and is out for the remainder of the season. That should mean more volume for Carnell Tate, when healthy. It also makes Elic Ayomanor an upside stash worth grabbing off the waiver wire, if he is still available in your league.

stories.headline: Hirving Lozano returns to San Diego FC as LA Galaxy loan ends
stories.summary: The LA Galaxy declined to exercise their purchase option for Hirving 'Chucky' Lozano, sending the Mexican forward back to San Diego FC.
stories.body:
LA Galaxy announced the club will not exercise the option to permanently acquire Hirving "Chucky" Lozano after his loan spell, as the forward returns to San Diego FC ahead of the 2027 sprint season.

"Hirving Lozano has completed his loan with the Galaxy and returned to his parent club, San Diego FC," the Galaxy announced in a press release when it made its 2026 roster decisions public.

The Galaxy signed Lozano on loan as a Designated Player in August through December 2026, with a permanent trade option included in the contract. He played 10 matches for the club, recording two goals and one assist, before the Galaxy made the decision to end his time with the club.

Lozano originally signed with San Diego FC in June 2025 while still under contract with PSV Eindhoven, months ahead of the expansion team's MLS debut. He finally joined the club in January, playing 27 matches in their inaugural season before conflict led him to the sidelines.

The Mexican forward was first left off the roster for San Diego FC's first-ever MLS playoff match following a report of a locker room altercation. Head coach Mikey Varas hinted that Lozano could be back with the team soon.

Lozano publicly apologized for his reaction inside the locker room before tensions escalated.

By January 2026, sporting director Tyler Heaps and Varas confirmed Lozano would no longer be taken into consideration.

"Our stance remains the same," sporting director Tyler Heaps told ESPN ahead of the team's 2026 season opener. "Hirving is not and will not be part of our sporting plans heading into this year."

Lozano trained independently for months before eventually signing with the Galaxy in August. It remains unclear what his role with San Diego will be in 2027 following his return from the loan spell.

The Galaxy also announced that veteran defender Maya Yoshida will depart after captaining the club for three and a half seasons. The Japan international made 117 appearances across all competitions and was a cornerstone of the squad that captured the club's sixth MLS Cup title in 2024.

stories.headline: Tom Brady tops list of athletes who became owners
stories.summary: The legendary quarterback is a member of an exclusive list of athletes that includes LeBron James, Serena Williams and Wayne Gretzky.
stories.body:
Tom Brady is getting (back) into the ownership game.

On Friday, sources confirmed to ESPN and NFL Network that the former superstar quarterback had bought shares in the English soccer giants Chelsea. Brady's purchasing of Chelsea shares comes after he departed the ownership group of another English club, EFL Championship side Birmingham City, earlier in the month after originally becoming a minority owner with a 3.3% stake.

Brady's latest interest isn't his only foray into the world of ownership -- he also owns a 5% minority stake in the Las Vegas Raiders, purchased in 2024, and he also has a stake in the Las Vegas Aces.

The NFL legend is far from the first athlete, active or former, to enter the ownership sphere. Here are other athletes who are now team owners:

Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Atlético Madrid

In October 26 news broke that the star Oklahoma City Thunder guard would be joining the club as an investor.

"I am excited to officially join the group of shareholders of Atlético de Madrid," Gilgeous-Alexander said in the club's post. "This is a club with a long history at the top of European football, and I am grateful for the opportunity to be part of its future."

Jason Kidd -- Everton

In April 2025, English Premier League club Everton announced that then-Dallas Mavericks coach Jason Kidd would be adding a different title to his résumé: ownership group member. The news came after Kidd joined Roundhouse Capital Holdings, which is part of the Friedkin Group -- the U.S. firm that completed its takeover of Everton's ownership the previous December.

Vince Carter, Tracy McGrady, Jozy Altidore -- Buffalo Bills

In December 2024, the Bills announced Carter, McGrady and Altidore were among 10 limited partners the team was adding to its ownership group. Both McGrady (New York Knicks) and Altidore (New York Red Bulls) played for New York-area teams, while Carter spent time with the Brooklyn Nets (who were known as the New Jersey Nets at the time) and was McGrady's teammate on the Toronto Raptors (who are closer to Buffalo than NYC-based teams).

Tom Brady -- Las Vegas Aces, Las Vegas Raiders, Chelsea

The Las Vegas Aces, the reigning WNBA champions, have added to their championship credentials. Seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady acquired a minority stake in the team whose majority owner is Las Vegas Raiders owner Mark Davis.

"I have always been a huge fan of women's sports, and I admire the work that the Aces' players, staff, and the WNBA continue to do to grow the sport and empower future generations of athletes," Brady said in a statement. "To be able to contribute in any way to that mission as a member of the Aces organization is an incredible honor."

Brady attended an Aces game in May 2022 and sent gifts to star Kelsey Plum. Plum and other Aces players were excited to have Brady as part of the team.

He also added the Las Vegas Raiders to his resume after his purchase of minority stake in the franchise was approved by NFL teams owners on Tuesday. The deal was agreed on in May 2023, but it took owners 17 months to give their approval over concerns he was receiving too much of a discount from majority owner Mark Davis.

Brady was also a minority owner of Birmingham City, a club in English soccer's second-tier Championship, but sold his shares in November 2026. He purchased shares in Chelsea later that month.

Lewis Hamilton -- Denver Broncos

The Broncos' ownership group added racing royalty in August 2022. Formula One driver Lewis Hamilton has a stake with the Walton-Penner group, which purchased the team in June 2022.

Hamilton, 37, has the Formula One record for most race wins and has won the Formula One title seven times. The ownership group, which purchased the team for $4.65 billion, is led by Walmart heir Rob Walton and includes former U.S. Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice, who also has a stake.

In April, Hamilton joined with Serena Williams in a consortium led by former Liverpool chairman Martin Broughton in an attempt to buy Premier League club Chelsea.

"He is a champion competitor who knows what it takes to lead a winning team," Walton said in a statement.

Marshawn Lynch -- Seattle Kraken

Lynch spent 13 seasons in Seattle with the Seahawks, but his new sports venture in the state of Washington is on the ice. On April 18, he joined the Seattle Kraken ownership team as a minority investor. The former NFL running back will be a part of the NHL's "Hockey is for Everyone" campaign and Kraken owner Tod Leiweke said Lynch expressed interest in shadowing him to learn hockey CEO operations.

"This is something I never would have imagined," Lynch said to CNBC in a statement. "I always dreamed of playing on a professional team but owning one is something special. As I look back on some of my accomplishments...I'm [going to] continue to count my blessings."

Grammy Award-winning artist and Seattle native Macklemore also joined the Kraken ownership team with Lynch.

Wayne Gretzky, Steve Nash and Dustin Johnson -- Las Vegas Desert Dogs

Wayne Gretzky is a big lacrosse guy? Yep, you read that right. The Great One may have made his name on the ice, but before Gretzky was the pride of the Edmonton Oilers he was a bona fide lax bro.

"The national sport of Canada is box lacrosse," Gretzky said. "I started playing lacrosse on a team at the age of six and played all the way until I was 16 years old. I have a great love for the game in the sense I really think that box lacrosse was such a crucial part of the success I ultimately had in ice hockey."

Because of this, it shouldn't be completely surprising that the hockey legend is linking up with 2020 Masters champion Dustin Johnson, NBA Hall of Famer and current Brooklyn Nets head coach Steve Nash and Nets owner Joe Tsai as part of a star-studded ownership group for the National Lacrosse League's newest expansion team in Las Vegas, the Desert Dogs.

Dwyane Wade -- Utah Jazz

Seeing Dwyane Wade support any team other than the Miami Heat is decidedly jarring. In April, the three-time NBA champion purchased an ownership stake in the Utah Jazz, joining majority owner and team governor Ryan Smith, and expressed a desire to take an active role in the franchise. D. Wade made good on his promise. He could be seen courtside throughout the season; he took action when an unsettling fan incident went down during the postseason, and he became a mentor to then-Jazz star Donovan Mitchell.

The former Miami Heat star also added to his portfolio with something a bit closer to home. Wade, a Chicago native, joined the ownership group of the WNBA's Chicago Sky.

"It's a great opportunity to be a part of the league in its very early stages. ... Growth is going to happen, and so I want to be a part of the growth of this league," Wade said.

Kevin Durant -- Philadelphia Union, NJ/NY Gotham FC

In June 2020, Brooklyn Nets star Kevin Durant purchased a 5% stake in MLS' Philadelphia Union, and he has an option to purchase an additional 5% at a later date. Durant also had engaged in talks about purchasing part of D.C. United the year prior, but he said the discussion never progressed.

Durant expanded his portfolio in May of this year, after being named as a minority owner of the National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) club NJ/NY Gotham FC.

Thirty Five Ventures (35V), a company co-founded by the two-time NBA champion and entrepreneur Rich Kleiman, made a significant investment to acquire a stake in the club, marking the company's second investment in a professional soccer team.

Renee Montgomery -- Atlanta Dream

Former Atlanta Dream guard Renee Montgomery made history in February as part of a three-member investor group that was approved to purchase the team. Montgomery is the first former player to become both an owner and executive of a WNBA franchise. The ownership change followed pressure on former Republican Sen. Kelly Loeffler to sell her share of the Dream, after she angered WNBA players with her opposition to the league's racial justice initiatives.

Patrick Mahomes -- Kansas City Royals

Patrick Mahomes is no stranger to winning. While the Kansas City Royals can't exactly say the same, you can't rule out that the quarterback's winning ways might rub off on the franchise now that he is part of their ownership group. If Mahomes' status as an icon in Kansas City was in question (it wasn't), this move surely cemented it. Becoming a baseball owner made sense on several levels for the Chiefs' QB1. Not only was Mahomes -- who played baseball in college -- a legitimate pro prospect, his father, Pat Mahomes, spent 11 seasons in Major League Baseball. He also had to find some way to put that $503 million contract extension to good use.

Venus and Serena Williams -- Miami Dolphins, Angel City FC

Winning major titles and making history, that's what the Williams sisters do. In 2009, Venus and Serena became the first Black female minority owners in the NFL by purchasing a part of the Miami Dolphins. Musicians Jimmy Buffett, Gloria and Emilio Estefan, Fergie and Marc Anthony also bought shares in the team -- the Dolphins' ownership group is nothing if not eclectic. Then, last year, Serena Williams became part of the star-studded Angel City FC ownership group bringing a NWSL team to Los Angeles in 2022.

Mia Hamm, Abby Wambach and Julie Foudy -- Angel City FC

When Angel City FC arrived on the scene it did so in style. Before we even knew the Los Angeles based NWSL club's name, we knew it had superstar backing like no other. Among the 14 former USWNT players who are part of the group are Mia Hamm, Abby Wambach and Julie Foudy. I would have named Lauren Holiday, Shannon Boxx, Rachel Buehler, Amanda Cromwell, Joy Fawcett, Tisha Venturini Hoch, Angela Hucles, Shannon MacMillan, Saskia Webber and sisters Lorrie Fair Allen and Ronnie Fair Sullins, but I was really trying to stay true to my whole "I'm only going to name 20 athletes" thing from the intro. There are also a bunch of celebrities in the mix, but we don't have that kind of time.

Michael Jordan -- Charlotte Hornets

While we're on the subject of owners who haven't had the type of success we grew accustomed to in their playing days, I would be remiss if I didn't mention the GOAT. In 2010, Michael Jordan became the first ex-player to be a majority owner in the league when the NBA's Board of Governors unanimously approved his $275 million bid to buy the then Charlotte Bobcats in his home state of North Carolina. After a decade of underwhelming years, things look to be on the up for the now Hornets with Rookie of the Year LaMelo Ball providing a long-awaited spark in the organization. Never forget when his dad said he could beat MJ one-on-one ... good times.

Alex Rodriguez -- Minnesota Timberwolves, Minnesota Lynx

I don't know what part of this purchase feels less ideal to me, that Alex Rodriguez and his 50-50 business partner Marc Lore are only pursuing acquiring the Minnesota Timberwolves and Lynx after their original plan to buy the New York Mets failed or that Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards had no idea who former MLB star A-Rod was. Either way, the $1.5 billion deal is expected to close around July 1.

David Beckham -- Inter Miami

David Beckham, iconic soccer player and remains-to-be-seen owner. Beckham -- who is incredibly hands on with the franchise -- is part of an ownership group which was initially called Miami Beckham United but now operates under the name Miami Freedom Park LLC. Beckham and Inter Miami have seemingly been riddled with controversy since the club's inception in 2018. But all those problems could be a thing of the past if Lionel Messi decides to head to MLS. Hey, stranger things have happened.

LeBron James -- Liverpool

Back in 2011, LeBron James and manager Maverick Carter became minority owners of Premier League club Liverpool after Fenway Sports Group, which purchased the team in 2010, became the sole marketer of James' global rights. The deal has turned out to be pretty lucrative for James -- his original stake in the club, valued at about $6.5 million, had grown to about $32 million as of 2018. In 2019, Liverpool won the Premier League for their first top-flight league title in thirty years.

James Harden -- Houston Dynamo, Houston Dash

James Harden might not be in Houston anymore, but the former Rockets superstar's presence is still felt in the city. The Beard purchased a 5% stake in the group that controls MLS' Houston Dynamo and NWSL's Houston Dash in 2019. Boxer Oscar De La Hoya is also part of the group. The Dash won their first NWSL title last year, so he's probably feeling pretty good about that investment.

Russell Wilson and Ken Griffey Jr. -- Seattle Sounders

What do Russell Wilson, Ken Griffey Jr. and Macklemore have in common? They are all part of the Seattle Sounders' ownership group. Wilson, along with his wife, musician Ciara, purchased a stake in the team in 2019 -- just in time for them to win an MLS Cup title. Griffey Jr. and his family followed suit in November 2020.

Zlatan Ibrahimovic -- Hammaraby

Seemingly everything Zlatan does makes people react intensely, and that remained true when he purchased part of Swedish team Hammaraby back in 2019. Fans of Malmo, another Swedish team where Zlatan started his professional career, reacted by vandalizing a statue of Zlatan outside the team's home stadium, placing a toilet seat around one of its arms.

Magic Johnson -- Los Angeles Dodgers

Big LA guy. In 2012, Lakers great Magic Johnson was part of a group that bought the Los Angeles Dodgers from Frank McCourt for a record $2 billion. At the time, the price shattered the mark for a sports franchise. Magic kept it real at the time of purchase when explaining his role in recruiting free agents, saying that while he can't talk hitting or pitching with players, he "can talk winning." If recent history is any indication (in case you blacked out all of 2020 -- the Dodgers won the World Series), it worked.

stories.headline: Champions League upstarts Como suffer Moise Kean injury blow
stories.summary: Como forward Moise Kean is set to be out injured for at least two months and could miss Champions League games against Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona.
stories.body:
Como forward Moise Kean is set to be out injured for at least two months, his coach Cesc Fabregas said on Friday, and could miss Champions League games against Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona.

The 26-year-old Italy forward injured his right leg against Belgium in the Nations League this week but the latest issue was with his left leg, Fabregas said.

- Meet Como's Nico Paz, the heir to Lionel Messi's No. 10 shirt for Argentina

- UCL talking points: First upsetting United, now NINE goals!? Are Como the real deal?

Como previously said Kean needed treatment on an injury in practice after returning from national team duty.

In its first season in the Champions League, Como have adapted stunningly fast with a 9-1 win at Lens and a pair of 4-1 victories at home to Manchester United and RB Leipzig.

Como are fourth in the 36-team standings ahead of hosting AEK Athens on Tuesday. The league phase for Como finishes with Real Betis next month and titleholders PSG, one of Kean's former clubs, and Barcelona in back-to-back weeks in January.

Kean arrived at Como on an initial season-long loan from Fiorentina and his injury leaves just Tasos Douvikas as a proven striker until the January transfer window. Kean has been limited to just four appearances for Como so far this season.

Como are fifth in Serie A and host Cagliari on Saturday.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Which NHL players scored the most points in a single season?
stories.summary: Connor McDavid looks to join Wayne Gretzky with a 200-point season.
stories.body:
Wayne Gretzky is the king of many NHL records. With points scored, Gretzky holds eight of the top 10 spots for most in a single season. He's also the only player to score 200 points in a season. Could Connor McDavid be the one to finally join him?

The Edmonton Oilers star started off the 2026-27 NHL season on a tear, finishing October at a 222-point pace. Gretzky's best year in points came in 1985-86, when he notched 215 from 52 goals and 163 assists.
