stories.headline: Kayla Harrison, Amanda Nunes reclaim leading roles in women's P4P top 10
stories.summary: Who do Kayla Harrison and Amanda Nunes replace in ESPN's P4P women's top 10?
stories.body:
Hello (again), Kayla Harrison and Amanda Nunes. Goodbye (for now), Valentina Shevchenko and Zhang Weili. The top of the ESPN women's MMA pound-for-pound rankings has a new look.

Harrison and Nunes, both of whom had been ineligible for the top 10 because of inactivity, returned over the weekend for a clash of elites at UFC 334. Harrison, defending her bantamweight championship for the first time after nearly a year and a half out of the cage while healing from surgery for herniated discs in her neck, scored a fourth-round submission of Nunes, who had been retired for nearly 3½ years. As a result, Harrison takes over the No. 1 ranking and Nunes, a former two-division champion and the consensus GOAT of women's MMA, is No. 2.

The former occupants of those spots, Shevchenko and Zhang, are newly ineligible for the rankings because it's been over a year since they have fought and they have nothing scheduled. Those two former champions drop out, and the rest of the women's top 10 remains the same.

In the men's rankings, UFC heavyweight champion Ciryl Gane moves up one spot to No. 7 on the strength of his decision win over Josh Hokit in their title bout at UFC 334.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Nov. 18. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Kayla Harrison

UFC bantamweight champion

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 20-1

Last: W (Sub4) vs. Amanda Nunes, Nov. 14

Next: TBA

Harrison stepped into the Octagon at UFC 334 already a reigning champion, but her submission win over Nunes was truly her crowning achievement. The backstory about their shared training gym history added drama to the buildup, but what mattered most about this matchup was that Harrison, who had voiced her goal to be the greatest ever in women's MMA, was facing the woman who has lived up to that standard. After choking out Nunes, what can Harrison do for an encore? Can any other woman in the sport give her a fight? Maybe it won't come to that. Harrison and Nunes both called for a rematch -- but at featherweight. That would lessen Harrison's burden in dealing with her toughest foe: the weigh-in scale.

2. Amanda Nunes

UFC bantamweight

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 23-6

Last: L (Sub4) vs. Kayla Harrison, Nov. 14

Next: TBA

Nunes' return from retirement did not go as she had hoped, but her failing was not so much about deteriorated physical abilities as it was about her ill-advised choice to venture too much into the grappling wheelhouse of Harrison, a two-time Olympic judo gold medalist. If Nunes gets the rematch both women are calling for, but this time at 145 pounds, that would seem to be to the advantage of Harrison, the bigger woman. But a redo would give Nunes another opportunity to lean into her own prodigious strength as a striker.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight champion

Record: 21-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Wang Cong, Oct. 3

Next: TBA

Silva was looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Rose Namajunas at UFC 324. And now she has fulfilled that expectation, beating Wang at UFC 332 to win the belt vacated by injured Valentina Shevchenko. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027.

5. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Record: 13-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Virna Jandiroba, Nov. 7

Next: TBA

If Suarez was still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Loopy Godínez. Then she went on to beat another fellow top-10 strawweight, Jandiroba, sending a message to the division that Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

8. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

9. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

10. Jasmine Jasudavicius

UFC flyweight

Record: 16-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Erin Blanchfield, Oct. 17

Next: TBA

Jasudavicius was rising in the 125-pound division until being knocked out by Manon Fiorot last year, halting a five-fight winning streak. But she got back up and won two in a row, most recently an impressive grappling performance against Blanchfield, to reassert herself as a contender.

Other fighter receiving votes: Joselyne Edwards and Virna Jandiroba.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Kayla Harrison; 2. Amanda Nunes; 3. Mackenzie Dern; 4. Natalia Silva; 5. Tatiana Suarez; 6. Cris Cyborg; 7. Alexa Grasso; 8. Manon Fiorot; 9. Dakota Ditcheva; 10. Virna Jandiroba.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Harrison; 2. Cyborg; 3. Silva; 4. Nunes; 5. Dern; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Suarez; 9. Fiorot; 10. Jasmine Jasudavicius.

Andrew Davis: 1. Harrison; 2. Nunes; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Dern; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Fiorot; 9. Suarez; 10. Jasudavicius.

Dre Waters: 1. Harrison; 2. Cyborg; 3. Nunes; 4. Dern; 5. Silva; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Suarez; 9. Fiorot; 10. Joselyne Edwards.

Jeff Wagenheim: 1. Harrison; 2. Nunes; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Grasso; 6. Dern; 7. Fiorot; 8. Suarez; 9. Ditcheva; 10. Jasudavicius.

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 29-4

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Movsar Evloev, Oct. 24

Next: TBA

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (38) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. He did just that by handing Evloev his first loss at UFC 333.

3. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 21-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Oct. 24

Next: TBA

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career, then completing his trilogy with Dvalishvili with a successful title defense. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet.

4. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

5. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

6. Joshua Van

UFC flyweight champion

Record: 18-2

Last: W (UD) vs. Alexandre Pantoja, Sept. 19

Next: Jan. 30 vs. Manel Kape

Van has been champion since December, but until UFC 331, there were doubters. Van had been handed the belt by default, when his challenge for the title was waved off after 26 seconds because Pantoja dislocated his left elbow. Van went on to defend the title against Tatsuro Taira in May, then faced Pantoja in a rematch at UFC 331. Van produced a clear victory -- his eighth win in a row -- to leave no doubt who rules at 125 pounds.

7. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight champion

Previous ranking: Tied for 8th

Record: 15-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Josh Hokit, Nov. 14

Next: TBA

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight on the White House lawn. Gane was elevated to undisputed champ after Aspinall, still injured, vacated his title, and the new champ made his first defense against Hokit at UFC 334, winning a slugfest.

8. Arman Tsarukyan

UFC lightweight

Previous ranking: 7

Record: 24-3

Last: W (KO1) vs. Mauricio Ruffy, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Tsarukyan is right back in the place he was in January 2025 -- on the cusp of a title fight. He withdrew from a challenge of Islam Makhachev one day before UFC 311 because of a back injury, and later in the year he was passed over twice when the UFC was booking lightweight title bouts. But by knocking out Ruffy with an elbow in the first round at UFC 331, Tsarukyan put himself back at the front of the line.

9. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Previous ranking: Tied for 8th

Record: 21-6

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Oct. 24

Next: TBA

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. Their third meeting at UFC 333 was the most competitive in their trilogy, but Dvalishvili fell short again.

10. Alex Pereira

UFC heavyweight

Record: 13-4

Last: L (TKO2) vs. Ciryl Gane, June 14

Next: Dec. 12 vs. Sergei Pavlovich

Pereira made a big splash in the MMA after a world championship career in kickboxing. He joined the UFC in 2021 and became a middleweight champion the following year, then moved on to be a two-time light heavyweight titlist before making an unprecedented bid for a belt in a third weight class when he fought Game at UFC Freedom 250 for an interim heavyweight title. Pereira got knocked out in that fight, but now he's back on his feet and in position to reclaim his position when he faces a fellow title contender, Pavlovich, at UFC 335.

Other fighters receiving votes: Alexandre Pantoja and Sean Strickland.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Islam Makhachev; 2. Petr Yan; 3. Ilia Topuria; 4. Alexander Volkanovski; 5. Joshua Van; 6. Arman Tsarukyan; 7. Merab Dvalishvili; 8. Ciryl Gane; 9. Alex Pereira; 10. Justin Gaethje.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Makhachev; 2. Volkanovski; 3. Gaethje; 4. Topuria; 5. Gane; 6. Yan; 7. Van; 8. Pereira; 9. Dvalishvili; 10. Tsarukyan.

Andrew Davis: 1. Makhachev; 2. Volkanovski; 3. Yan; 4. Gaethje; 5. Topuria; 6. Van; 7. Gane; 8. Tsarukyan; 9 Pereira; 10. Sean Strickland.

Dre Waters: 1. Makhachev; 2. Volkanovski; 3. Yan; 4. Gaethje; 5. Topuria; 6. Van; 7. Dvalishvili; 8. Gane; 9. Pereira; 10. Tsarukyan.

Jeff Wagenheim: 1. Makhachev; 2. Yan; 3. Volkanovski; 4. Van; 5. Gaethje; 6. Tsarukyan; 7. Topuria; 8. Gane; 9. Dvalishvili; 10. Alexandre Pantoja.

stories.headline: Kangaroos bounce Kiwis for fourth-straight Rugby League World Cup title
stories.summary: The Kangaroos have won a fourth-straight Rugby League World Cup, toppling New Zealand 32-12 in Brisbane.
stories.body:
The Kangaroos have punished a disappointing New Zealand, with Reece Walsh running riot in a 32-12 World Cup final waltz.

There was an expectation the Kiwis, searching for their second Cup title and first since 2008, would push Australia all the way after a two-point loss in a pulsating tournament opener.

But the visitors struggled from the outset in Brisbane on Sunday night, Jamayne Isaako's kick-off floating long in a sign of things to come.

Walsh dazzled at fullback for the Kangaroos, his pace, vision and wicked footwork too much as he helped lay on two tries and generally wreak havoc around the ruck and close to the line.

Conversely, Walsh's New Zealand opposite Kalyn Ponga -- International Rugby League's Golden Boot winner on Thursday night -- was unable to get into game.

Australian hooker Harry Grant and halves Tom Dearden and Cam Munster completely outplayed their error-riddled opposites, while the Kangaroos' pack muscled up.

Dearden laid on two first-half tries for Liam Martin with well-timed short balls, while Bradman Best was rewarded for an inspired chase-down tackle of Jahrome Hughes with a try soon after.

When Tom Trbojevic scored to begin the second half it was 28-6 and effectively game over.

Jack Bostock completed his breakout season with a try in each half for Australia.

It was the Kangaroos' fourth consecutive title and 10th in the last 11 tournaments, dating back to 1975.

stories.headline: Russell reignites Verstappen rivalry: 'Somebody has got to stand up to that guy'
stories.summary: The rivalry between Max Verstappen and George Russell reignited on the streets of Las Vegas on Friday evening after Russell claimed the Red Bull driver thinks he is "bigger and better than everyone else."
stories.body:
The rivalry between Max Verstappen and George Russell reignited on the streets of Las Vegas on Friday evening after Russell claimed the Red Bull driver thinks he is "bigger and better than everyone else."

Verstappen and Russell, who have been involved in multiple incidents together over the years, will start next to each other on the front row of the grid for Saturday evening's race.

The pair have already banged wheels this weekend after they found themselves fighting over the same piece of Las Vegas' famous Strip during final practice.

As the pair prepared for flying laps, Verstappen passed Russell ahead of Turn 14 at the end of the Strip, which led to Russell repassing him in the braking zone.

The Mercedes driver felt the start of his next lap would be compromised by Verstappen being ahead of him, but as he attempted to move back past the Red Bull, he was squeezed to the inside of the track by Verstappen.

By the time the two cars reached the apex of Turn 14, there was not enough space for them to make the corner without contact and Verstappen was forced to the edge of the track, where he had to back out of the throttle.

Russell and Verstappen were summoned to the stewards after practice and the Red Bull driver was given a formal warning for his "unpredictable" change of direction under braking.

In the qualifying session that followed, Verstappen finished second fastest ahead of Russell in third, but those positions will become first and second for Saturday's grid once an engine penalty for Kimi Antonelli, who was fastest overall in qualifying, is applied.

- Max Verstappen promoted to Las Vegas GP pole as Kimi Antonelli drops to sixth

- Hamilton and Leclerc suffer shock Ferrari double blow in Las Vegas qualifying

- George Russell and Max Verstappen make contact in final Las Vegas practice

Speaking after qualifying, Russell said he did not believe Verstappen deserved a grid penalty for their collision but made clear that he would not back down against the four-time world champion.

"Well, I mean, the warning was fine," Russell told Sky Sports Italy. "There's nothing in the rules to say that you cannot overtake someone who is starting their lap, but when you do this, you are screwing this person over.

"He does this week in, week out, with many drivers. Everybody accepts it and I am not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this and walk around like they are bigger and better than everyone else. Somebody has got to stand up to that guy."

While he sat on the same sofa as Russell during the post-qualifying news conference in Las Vegas, Verstappen refused to acknowledge the incident in practice.

"Nothing happened," he said when asked to comment on the collision and subsequent investigation by the stewards.

At the Mexico City Grand Prix last month, Verstappen was involved in a similar free practice incident with Liam Lawson for which both drivers were given one-place grid penalty.

But the stewards in Las Vegas did not feel Friday's incident was serious enough to warrant a sporting penalty.

"The stewards considered that Car 3's [Verstappen's] change of direction under braking was unpredictable and contributed to the situation in which Car 63 [Russell] had to move to the inside to avoid contact," a statement said. "While the stewards did not consider the maneuver sufficiently serious to warrant a more severe penalty, they concluded that changing direction under braking in these circumstances fell below the standard of driving expected.

"Taking into account the circumstances of the incident, the Stewards determined that a driver warning was appropriate."

Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff said he was looking forward to the next instalment of Russell versus Verstappen in Saturday's race.

"Big cinema," he told Sky Sports when asked what to expect from the two drivers on the front row of the grid. "If they try to go through the first corners together, we shall be watching."

stories.headline: Nikola Jokic's big 2nd half sends the Nuggets to a 133-124 win over the Rockets
stories.summary: — Nikola Jokic had 26 points, 11 assists and seven rebounds as the Denver Nuggets defeated the Houston Rockets 133-124 in a back-and-forth NBA Cup game Friday night.
stories.body:
DENVER -- — Nikola Jokic had 26 points, 11 assists and seven rebounds as the Denver Nuggets defeated the Houston Rockets 133-124 in a back-and-forth NBA Cup game Friday night.


Christian Braun and Cameron Johnson each scored 19 for the Nuggets in a matchup that featured 32 lead changes and 17 ties. Neither team led by more than five until there was 2:01 remaining.


The win was Denver's sixth in eight games, the past two of which have come against the Rockets and Boston Celtics, who are a combined 23-9.


Aaron Gordon added 18 points for the Nuggets, while DeMar DeRozan scored 15 and Jamal Murray had 14 points and seven assists. Jokic scored 24 points in the second half, including 18 in the third quarter.


Alperen Sengun, who played the first quarter in goggles after sustaining a scratched cornea in a win Wednesday against Indiana, led the way for Houston with 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists for his second triple-double this season.


Each of the Rockets’ starters finished with at least 16 points, including 25 from Fred VanVleet, who also had nine assists. Their backups, however, provided only 12 points and combined to miss 13 of 17 shots.


After a 20-foot jumper by VanVleet extended Houston’s lead to five with 5:10 left, Denver countered with 10 straight points in 1:55 and finished the game on a 23-9 run.


The Nuggets improved to 2-0 in the group stage of the NBA Cup, while the Rockets dropped to 1-2.


It was the second meeting in 11 days between the teams. Houston won the first one, 110-100, on Nov. 9.


Up next
Rockets: Host the Los Angeles Clippers on Monday.


Nuggets: At the Chicago Bulls on Sunday.

stories.headline: Dodgers acquire infielder Royce Lewis in trade with Twins
stories.summary: The Dodgers acquired infielder Royce Lewis in a trade with the Twins, fulfilling Los Angeles' need for a versatile right-handed hitter to replace Miguel Rojas.
stories.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers acquired talented, oft-injured infielder Royce Lewis in a trade with the Minnesota Twins on Friday, fulfilling their need for a versatile right-handed hitter to replace the retiring Miguel Rojas.

Bobby Miller, a former prized starter who recently transitioned to the bullpen, is going to the Twins along with 19-year-old catching prospect Francisco Espinoza.

Lewis, 27, is projected by MLB Trade Rumors to make $5.1 million in arbitration in his second-to-last year before free agency and was a threat to be non-tendered ahead of Friday's deadline. In L.A., though, he fits precisely what the Dodgers were searching for this offseason: a right-handed hitter who can occasionally spell the left-handed-hitting Max Muncy and Freddie Freeman at first base while also drawing starts at second base.

Lewis spent ample time at all three of those positions with the Twins in 2026 while batting .227/.287/.380 with 15 home runs and 16 stolen bases in 125 games.

The 2017 No. 1 overall pick out of high school in San Juan Capistrano, California -- located 60 miles south of Dodger Stadium -- Lewis has mostly been defined by the injuries that robbed him of stardom. He debuted as a 22-year-old in 2022, but injuries to his right knee, oblique, hamstring and quad limited him to only 152 games over a three-year period -- during which he carried an 0.825 OPS with 33 home runs and 104 RBIs.

Lewis stayed mostly healthy in 2025 and 2026, totaling 231 games, but he produced 15% below the league average, according to OPS-plus.

By trading Lewis and not tendering offers to outfielder Trevor Larnach and right-handed starter Bailey Ober, the Twins lopped off approximately $18.3 million in payroll Friday.

Miller, 27, broke out as a starter in 2023, going 11-4 with a 3.76 ERA while showcasing a triple-digit fastball and a vicious curveball. He struggled mightily in the majors and minors over the next two years, however, and missed almost the entirety of the 2026 season with a shoulder injury.

stories.headline: 'No one saw it coming': Inside the Swans' draft heist that landed a Lions Academy star
stories.summary: The Swans are notorious for bidding on draft night. But no one saw their heist of Lions Academy star Caylen Murray coming, given they didn't even meet his family. Jasper Chellappah looks into the fascinating happenings on night one of the AFL Draft.
stories.body:
Caylen Murray is the earliest pick to have his club-tied matching rights passed up in AFL Draft history. No one saw it coming, not even the Lions.

Make no mistake, this was a Sydney draft heist months in the making. The Swans ran the numbers and it showed Brisbane was three misly points short of matching a bid at pick 9. They pulled the trigger and watched on for five agonising minutes as trade partners disappeared one by one.

The three-time premiers were scrambling and the scenes unfolding inside their corporate box were increasingly uncomfortable. Each phone call was shorter than the last as candidates dried up in a race against time to find three points.

Up until that stage Sydney had not shown serious interest in Murray. They surely wouldn't bid on him without any leaks of interest from their camp; they surely couldn't bid on him without meeting his family.

A smokescreen devised in pre-draft analysis and 12 months of assessing Murray's talents was pulled at the perfect time to rip him out of Queensland. They feigned disinterest and caught the Lions napping. No one saw it coming, not least Brisbane's war room.

'Bidney' has been up to these tricks before. They'd made 11 bids in 10 years prior to last night, including Brisbane's own prospect Sam Marshall. They nearly snared Adelaide's Max Michalanney with a similar ploy in 2022.

As the dust settles, it's clear to see the Lions were undone by new draft rules that they themselves necessitated.

In 2022 they used 34, 35, 38, 40, and 41 to match Will Ashcroft's bid at pick 2. In 2024 they used 40, 42, 43, and 46 to match Levi Ashcroft's bid at pick 5. In 2025 they used 22, 23, and 39 to match a bid at pick 6 for Dan Annable. They achieved similar results for first-round talents Jaspa Fletcher and Marshall.

Brisbane had played the system to perfection up until Thursday night. But new draft rules require clubs to find the points to match with a maximum of two draft picks. A new draft value index (DVI) inflated the worth of top 10 picks. And a new levy added a 20% tax to bids matched by grand finalists.

Brisbane was caught looking too far ahead by sliding pick 19 down to 24 and 34. The 1355-point value of pick 9 became 1626 points with the grand finalist loading. Brisbane's picks 24 and 25 were worth 1211 points and they could go into a maximum of 412 points deficit on their future first-rounder. Tallied up and they accounted for 1623 of the 1626 points required.

The AFL values that gap at 1/1000th of the worth of the 3000 points Dougie Cochrane was matched with.

Sydney pulled off a coup to rival footy's very best off-field drama in 2026.

Brisbane's shortcoming wasn't just to the Swans's benefit, either. Gustavo Teixeira landed in St Kilda's lap at pick 11, a genuine pick one chance throughout the season. The flow-on effect kept coming with Collingwood grabbing their top target in mad Pies fan Sam Gayfer. Without the bid being matched these clubs effectively moved up the draft order.

Murray's shock was plain to see as reality set in. But the star academy graduate quickly recovered to deliver an extremely mature interview.

"I didn't realise Sydney was that keen but [I'm] stoked to join the club. It's an amazing club, great players, great staff and I'm keen to explore Sydney.

"It was a bit of a shock at the start but now it's sunk in. I'm stoked to be a Swans player."

The classy and composed halfback looms as a natural replacement for departed All-Australian Nick Blakey.

A primetime game can be a perfect opportunity for a team to send a message with its play. It also helps when it is looking its finest on the gridiron. The Houston Texans and Washington Commanders enter Week 10 with one part of that down with the debut of their respective uniforms.

It was the Texans' turn first, as they wore their Rivalries threads against the Indianapolis Colts on "Thursday Night Football." The look is primarily white, but includes H-Town blue and battle red with details that pay homage to Houston's streets. The city's signature blue street tiles appear on the uniform's helmet, name plate, sleeve, collar and pant stripes in a two-tone battle red and blue finish. Houston's "be someone" bridge is the inspiration for the blue jersey numbers.

For the first time, the Texans wore a liberty white helmet, paying tribute to the white prototype founder Robert C. McNair revealed in 1999 before shifting to a deep steel blue lid. The white helmet's face mask includes a chrome H-town blue finish, a nod to Houston's car culture.

stories.headline: Nashville coach Callaghan '100%' focused on playoffs amid USMNT links
stories.summary: BJ Callaghan said he remains fully focused on leading Nashville through the MLS playoffs amid links to replacing Mauricio Pochettino as USMNT head coach.
stories.body:
BJ Callaghan said he remains fully focused on leading Nashville SC through the Major League Soccer playoffs, amid links to replacing Mauricio Pochettino as United States men's national team head coach.

"For me, it's not about me. We've earned ourselves to get to the playoffs here and my job is to be a leader of this team and one of the leaders in this club," Callaghan told reporters on Friday.

- Pochettino: 'Massive' pressure with USMNT makes me better coach for Man United

- Ex-U.S. coach Arena: Federation doesn't 'have a clue' how to replace Poch

- MLS playoff Round 1 predictions: Who will move on to the conference semifinals?

"My focus is 100% on the players, the staff, the fans and overall this soccer club to make sure what happened in the regular season, we can make it an extension into the playoffs because we have more things to achieve here."

Pochettino departed his role as U.S. coach this week to become Manchester United's new coach. U.S. Soccer announced under-23 coach Steve Cherundolo will lead the team during the December international camp while the search for Pochettino's replacement is underway.

Callaghan previously served as an assistant to then-USMNT coach Gregg Berhalter before taking over interim charge in 2023. He led the group to the Concacaf Nations League title and reached the semifinals of the Gold Cup later that year before Berhalter was re-appointed.

Callaghan joined Nashville in 2024 and turned the team into a trophy-winning side.

Nashville lifted the U.S. Open Cup in 2025, when defeating Austin FC, and earned the 2026 MLS Supporters' Shield. Callaghan also inspired the Eastern Conference team to break the league's record for most points in a single season, with 77 points in 34 games, shattering Inter Miami's previous tally.

Nashville will now face FC Cincinnati in the best-of-three round one playoff series starting on Sunday.

Former Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Manchester City coach Pep Guardiola has been the biggest name linked to replacing Pochettino. Before his departure following a Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal win over Haiti on Tuesday, Pochettino encouraged anyone interested to take the job.

"It's the perfect moment to arrive to the [U.S. Soccer] Federation," Pochettino told reporters at a roundtable Monday. "Everything is in the right direction. I think, of course, take [it]. Take it because he's going to find really good people, good players. The player can fit for his style; the National Training Center that wasn't [there] before."

stories.headline: Revisiting sports and pop culture from GTA V's launch
stories.summary: "Grand Theft Auto VI" was released Thursday following a 13-year wait since GTA V.
stories.body:
Peyton Manning was beginning a record-setting season. Joel Embiid had yet to play a college basketball game. And "Breaking Bad" hadn't reached its finale.

That was 4,812 days ago, when "Grand Theft Auto V" arrived on Sept. 17, 2013.

More than 13 years later, "Grand Theft Auto VI" launches Thursday, with athletes and teams counting down to its release -- and looking back at how much has changed.

Houston Rockets center Steven Adams even quipped during media day that performances could be impacted by the game's release.

"So look at NFL, look at all the leagues and watch them plummet. Just for the month of November, performances are going to go down," Adams said.

Before finding out whether Adams' prediction holds up, here's a look at the sports and pop culture landscape when GTA V arrived -- Sept. 17, 2013.

Seattle and Denver were starting their Super Bowl runs

The NFL had just finished its second week and two squads were in the early stages of dominant campaigns: Seattle and Denver.

The Seahawks' defense proved to be its superpower, earning the "Legion of Boom" nickname. Seattle allowed 273.6 yards and 14.4 points per game, both the fewest in the regular season. The Broncos averaged a league-high 457.3 yards and 37.9 points per game, while Peyton Manning tossed an NFL record 5,477 yards plus 55 touchdowns.

Both teams would finish with 13-3 records, setting up a Super Bowl meeting in February 2014. Seattle would emerge victorious on the biggest stage after stifling Denver's offense in a 43-8 victory -- and the seeds of Super Bowl XLVIII were sprouting as GTA V was released.

Miami Heat looking to three-peat

The LeBron James, Dwyane Wade and Chris Bosh Big Three were entering their fourth season as teammates following back-to-back titles.

Miami edged out the San Antonio Spurs in the 2013 NBA Finals, an instant classic. The Heat faced a series clinching defeat in Game 6 before Ray Allen's late 3-pointer sent it into overtime. The extra period ended in a Miami victory to force a Game 7, where it closed out another championship.

The Heat faced the Spurs in a rematch in 2014, and San Antonio got its revenge this time around. But, for two straight summers, Miami reigned supreme.

Five stars preparing to go one-and-done

The 2013 college basketball freshman class had its fair share of heavy hitters.

In March 2013, then-high schoolers Andrew Wiggins and Jabari Parker graced the cover of Slam Magazine with the headline "Young Money: The game's next superstars have arrived." Wiggins and Parker were No. 1 and 2, respectively, in the SC Next rankings, but they were far from the only top prospects.

Joel Embiid, Julius Randle and Aaron Gordon all featured in the top 10 of the rankings as five-star prospects. Each of them, alongside Wiggins and Parker, went one-and-done and were selected in the top 10 of the 2014 NBA draft. Other notable names in the 2013 high school class included twins Aaron and Andrew Harrison, Noah Vonleh and Wayne Selden.

'Breaking Bad' nears its end as 'Roar' rules the charts

One of the greatest TV shows of all time, the final season of "Breaking Bad" aired as GTA V came out.

Two days before its release, the iconic "Ozymandias" episode aired. Series creator Vince Gilligan said that the episode is the "best episode we ever have had or ever will have." It remains one of the highest-rated episodes of the series on IMDB with 9.5 stars.

Pop songs led the way on the Billboard Hot 100 the week GTA V came out. Katy Perry's "Roar" hit No. 1 on Sept. 16, 2013, at the time matching Rihanna for the most No. 1's in the chart's 21-year history at 10. It took six weeks for "Roar" to reach No. 1, then-the fastest No. 1 hit since Perry's "California Gurls" in 2010.

Slotted in at No. 2 was "Blurred Lines" by Robin Thicke featuring T.I. and Pharrell. That track spent 10 weeks on the top before being dethroned. Lorde's "Royals" was at No. 3, while Jay-Z and Justin Timberlake's "Holy Grail" sat at No. 4.

The rest of the songs on the charts' top 10 included: "Wake Me Up!" by Avicii, "Summertime Sadness" by Lana Del Rey vs. Cedric Gervais, "Applause" by Lady Gaga, "Hold On, We're Going Home" by Drake featuring Majid Jordan, "Safe And Sound" by Capital Cities and "Berzerk" by Eminem.

WNBA, MLB teams were building championship legacies

The Minnesota Lynx won their second WNBA championship in 2013, and it would mark the beginning of a dynasty. Minnesota won two more in 2015 and 2017, the latter of which made it four titles in seven seasons as the club also won in 2011. Hall of Famer Maya Moore played a key role in each of the four championships. In 2013, she averaged 20.9 points on 53% shooting in the playoffs.

MLB saw similar dominance in alternating years from the San Francisco Giants. San Francisco missed the postseason in 2013 after World Series titles in 2010 and 2012. Someone privy to a trend could've predicted that the Giants would win it again in 2014 -- which they did. San Francisco hasn't won a World Series since, however.

BCS era coming to a close

College athletics looked entirely different 13 years ago, to say the least.

One of the biggest changes in college football lies in the implementation of the playoff system. Previously, the sport used the BCS rankings for 16 years to determine which two teams would play in the national championship game. That system had its fair share of controversies and came to a close following the 2013 campaign.

Florida State and Auburn made sure the BCS era went out with a bang at the Rose Bowl. Facing a four-point deficit with 1:05 left, Heisman-winning quarterback Jameis Winston led the Seminoles down the field for a game-winning touchdown. Two plays later Florida State closed it out to win 34-31 and clinch its first national championship since 1999 in memorable fashion.

stories.headline: Harry Kane sets sights on Champions League, England trophy after Ballon d'Or win
stories.summary: Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane is on a mission to claim trophies that have so far eluded him in his career, namely a Champions League and a tittle with England.
stories.body:
Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane is on a mission to claim trophies that have so far eluded him in his career, namely a Champions League crown with Bayern Munich and a tittle with England.

Kane, 33, lost in both the World Cup and Champions League semi-finals last season but was rewarded for his stellar campaign at Bayern and his performances with England this summer.

He had 61 goals in all competitions for Bayern and was the Bundesliga's top scorer with 36 goals.

Kane scored six times in seven appearances while captaining England to third place, their best finish at a World Cup since 1966.

Kane, who beat Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal to claim football's most prestigious individual award last month, told Footmercato: "Of course, I'd love to win another Ballon d'Or, but I know there are plenty of other great players in with a chance.

"But there are still lots of trophies I'd like to win, such as the Champions League with Bayern and, of course, a title with England."

"I am extremely proud to have won the Ballon d'Or, and receiving this award in my home town [London] made the moment even more special.

"To see my name alongside players such as R9 [Ronaldo Nazario] -- who, incidentally, presented the award to me that evening -- Cristiano Ronaldo, Lionel Messi and Gerd Müller is a source of immense pride, especially given my journey, which included loan spells early in my career that forced me to show self-belief and resilience."

The England captain credits his move to Bayern in the summer of 2023 from Tottenham as pivotal in his career.

"Since joining Bayern, I've clearly taken my game to the next level, and I feel I'm in the best form of my career," he said.

"I think winning the Ballon d'Or has changed the way people perceive me around the world. I'd probably underestimated the excitement and the fans' reaction.

"When I held up the trophy in front of the supporters waiting for me in the street as I left the ceremony, I realised I was experiencing a magical moment that I'll never forget. This victory reflects an exceptional season I've had, filled with goals, titles and memorable moments.

"Winning the Ballon d'Or at the age of 33 simply shows that if you keep working hard and believing in yourself, you can reach the very top."

- Harry Kane: England and Spain are 'the best teams in international football'

- Harry Kane stats: His most eye-opening England cap, goal records

- Kane thanks doctor who reinvigorated his career ahead of record-breaking 126th cap

Kane, who has won two consecutive league titles with Bayern, has his sight set on lifting the Champions League this season. He was close to doing so with Spurs in 2019 but lost 2-0 in the final to Liverpool.

Bayern have not won Europe's elite club competition since 2020 when they beat Paris Saint-Germain in the final, the team that eliminated them last season.

"The Champions League is a major goal for me and for the team," Kane said.

"We've got a strong squad, made up of incredible players. Last season, the matches against PSG were mad -- it was down to the wire -- and being knocked out by the team that won the title twice in a row was nothing to be ashamed of. Spending another year with the manager [Vincent Kompany] and the team is helping us to become even stronger.

"We went into this season telling ourselves that this had to be our year. We need to find a way to make it happen, find that little bit extra that will make the difference to get through the rounds, and do everything we can to win the Champions League. That's our main objective."

stories.headline: Abu Dhabi court reduces sentences for 8 in Nurmagomedov-Dvalishvili brawl
stories.summary: An Abu Dhabi court has reduced the sentences of eight defendants, including six members of Team Nurmagomedov, for their part in last week's wild hotel brawl in the UAE's capital city.
stories.body:
Abu Dhabi's Criminal Court has reduced the sentences of eight defendants convicted in connection to last week's hotel brawl involving Usman Nurmagomedov and Merab Dvalishvili, according to the Abu Dhabi Judicial Department.

The eight defendants, including six members of Team Nurmagomedov, were originally sentenced to six months in prison. Under the revised ruling, which the ADJD released Tuesday, each defendant will instead pay a fine of 150,000 AED (approximately $40,800). The department said the reduced sentence followed a reconciliation between the parties, the mutual withdrawal of claims and appeal by the victim to the Abu Dhabi government for their release.

The altercation took place Nov. 11 in the lobby of the Yas Hilton Hotel, ahead of RAF's inaugural event in Abu Dhabi. Multiple videos captured Nurmagomedov, who is the PFL lightweight champion and younger cousin of Khabib Nurmagomedov, approach Dvalishvili from behind and slap him in the face, triggering a brawl between multiple members of both teams. Dvalishvili, who was initially arrested but released, advocated for Nurmagomedov's release Saturday.

Nurmagomedov and Dvalishvili have been involved in a long-running feud, dating back to Dvalishvili's UFC title win against Umar Nurmagomedov, Usman's older brother, in January 2025. The camps were involved in a brief altercation at another RAF event in July in Dvalishvili's home country of Georgia. Over the weekend, UFC president Dana White criticized RAF's security measures, saying, "They must like it for this to happen all the time."

RAF founder Chad Bronstein told ESPN the organization regretted the incident, but pushed back on any suggestion it's becoming commonplace.

"Did they have drama in the past? Yeah," Bronstein said of Nurmagomedov and Dvalishvili. "But did I think that was going to happen in Abu Dhabi? No. You can always expect there's going to be some words in a press conference ... I didn't think that would happen in a hotel lobby. How many fights have taken place at the UFC, at press conferences, in arenas? We have a great relationship with the UFC, but I think that's an unfair statement."

Bronstein added the incident did not impact RAF's recently-signed deal with the region of Abu Dhabi.

"We're already talking about new events coming up, we have a five-year deal," Bronstein said. "Saturday's event sold out Etihad Arena. I feel like there's going to be a long partnership."

On Monday, RAF announced Dvalishvili and his 21-year-old Georgian teammate Saba Lazishvili have been booked to the promotion's first event in the New York metropolitan area on Dec. 19 at Nassau Coliseum in Long Island.

Dvalishvili will face Kenzo Biyong, a former Dutch professional soccer player from the Netherlands. Lazashvili, who gained a massive online following for his participation in the hotel lobby brawl, will face the winner of a match between Sergio Garcia and Cody Garbrandt at RAF 15 on Nov. 28 in Chicago.

stories.headline: First-half romp powers Jillaroos' fourth-straight Rugby League World Cup salute
stories.summary: Australia's Jillaroos have blown away New Zealand 34-10 to win a fourth-straight Women's Rugby League World Cup.
stories.body:
Australia have underlined their women's rugby league dominance with a 34-10 annihilation of New Zealand in the World Cup final.

The Jillaroos did the damage with six first-half tries on Sunday at Suncorp Stadium, with winger Jaime Chapman recording a brilliant hat-trick before the break to cap a historic tournament.

It was Australia's fourth straight Cup triumph, following a 54-4 win in the final four years ago and coming after New Zealand won the first three tournaments between 2000-08.

Chapman carried two players more than 10 metres to score her first, before flying into the corner for another and then busting through four tacklers for a sensational 70-metre solo effort.

Her treble gave her the equal record for tries in a World Cup -- for men or women -- at 13, matching the Kiwi Ferns' Honey Hireme-Smiler from 2017.

It seemed inevitable that she would go clear in the second half.

But both teams struggled in the Brisbane humidity, with the Kiwi Ferns' try in the finals seconds the only points of an error-riddled second period.

For the Jillaroos there were several poignant narratives to come out of the win.

Coach Jess Skinner's controversial decision to play five-eighth Jesse Southwell and drop Jocelyn Kelleher paid dividends.

Southwell schemed with the ball, landed five goals and was the perfect foil for half Tarryn Aiken, who controlled play with confidence and skill.

Chapman played in the pool games and semi-final in the 2022 World Cup but has now put an indelible stamp on a final.

"There is no better win than winning the World Cup on home turf," she told Channel Seven.

"We connected the first day we came into camp."

Fullback Tamika Upton sat out the tournament four years ago with a calf injury but now the five-time premiership winner has every team accolade in the game to her credit.

Prop Millie Elliott retires with a fairytale ending while dual international Sariah Paki, who was chased by the Ferns to play for them, has now won the World Cup in two sports after triumphing with the Australian rugby sevens side in 2022.

All the talk before the clash was the danger posed by New Zealand's Golden Boot winner and strike centre Stacey Waaka.

The former rugby union star, who had scored nine tries in the tournament, was snuffed out by Jillaroos captain Isabelle Kelly, who confronted Waaka all match and gave her no space.

As the Jillaroos' big guns stood up, centre Jessica Sergis scored her 23rd try in 18 Tests with a 70m dash through the middle off an undetected forward pass.

Aiken turned second-rower Shaylee Bent inside for the second try of the match while Upton started and finished a movement that had her attacking fingerprints all over it.

Ferns fullback Apii Nicholls was her side's best player in a dynamic display until she tore a hamstring in the 66th minute.
